member.name: AbsBookMap
member.para: An item id is opaque, and its shape has moved. Checked against the project's test server (Audiobookshelf 2.36.0, 2026-08-30): every item id it reports is a plain UUID - 914ccbcc-ee3c-46c3-b018-62ba0c147823 for "Perry Rhodan Silber Edition 014: Rhodans Sohn" - and not the li_... form that older write-ups about Audiobookshelf show. Nothing here validates the shape and nothing should start: an entry's id is passed through to a catalogue lookup as written, so a server that spells ids differently again costs this code nothing. The consequence for the documentation is the part that nearly went wrong - doc\manual.md says the id is what Audiobookshelf's own address for a book ends in, and deliberately does not say what one looks like.

Why the separator is = and not the : its sibling uses. --custom-file reads phrase:title and can, because its left-hand side is either a bare word or a /regexp/ whose closing slash delimits. Here the right-hand side carries colons twice over: the item: prefix is one, and a library title routinely holds another - the corpus's own "Perry Rhodan Silber Edition 087: Das Spiel des Laren" is the example the manual uses. A colon separator would have needed a rule to decide which colon, and any such rule would be a guess about punctuation conventions - the same objection that sank the series-prefix tier in 's own notes.
